subject.title: refactor: prune unsupported OPENCLAW env overrides

question: Should OpenClaw remove these seven undocumented environment overrides now, accepting possible breakage for undiscovered external users, or preserve a temporary transition?
rationale: Source and repository searches support the cleanup, but code review cannot determine whether private operator automation relies on undocumented environment behavior; the protected label also requires explicit maintainer intent.

options.title: Land the bounded cleanup
options.body: Accept the narrow compatibility risk because no documentation, installer, workflow, extension, or repository caller establishes these aliases as supported contracts and canonical replacements remain available.

options.title: Add a transition period
options.body: Temporarily preserve selected aliases with explicit deprecation and removal criteria if maintainers know of external users or packaged deployments that depend on them.

recommendation.title: Land the bounded cleanup
recommendation.body: Accept the narrow compatibility risk because no documentation, installer, workflow, extension, or repository caller establishes these aliases as supported contracts and canonical replacements remain available.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the repository-level compatibility decision and authored both the audit and final implementation.
